analysis.title: October 2026: Month in review
key_insights: Global equities (MSCI AC World) fell 1.5% in October but are up 12.1% year to date. The S&P 500 fell 0.9% while the S&P 500 Equal Weight gained 5.0% (up 15.5% YTD), so the headline decline masked broadening leadership.

Higher energy prices, persistent inflation, rising bond yields and scrutiny of AI investment weighed on sentiment. Brent crude rose 13.0% in October, the fourth straight monthly gain, adding to concerns that inflation stays elevated for longer.

September US core inflation accelerated to 2.6% y/y from 2.4% in August, stronger than expected. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% in early October before reversing as tech weakness drove safe-haven demand and the Fed, ECB and BoJ held rates.
The Fed decision carried a mildly hawkish message. Officials upgraded their growth assessment from 'solid' to 'strong' and two policymakers favored an immediate rate increase.

AI investment scrutiny centered on three areas: overinvestment amid pressure on free cash flow, growing reliance on debt, equity, leases and supplier-backed financing, and the risk that new AI products displace established revenue before comparable monetization. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on the final trading day and 5.3% in October, its worst month since March 2025.

Q3 results showed AI demand remained robust. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y and Microsoft Azure grew 48%, with an eightfold increase in large Copilot accounts. Cloud growth accelerated across the largest providers and advance orders for computing capacity expanded.

UBS sees AI financing risk concentrated among specialized AI cloud providers (borrowing costs, construction delays, utilization, refinancing). Because most AI capex sits with larger, better-funded companies, UBS expects selective project delays, repricing and consolidation rather than a broad reversal in AI spending.

UBS expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 25-30%, supported by AI investment, an improving industrial cycle and consumption. It recommends staying invested in diversified cyclical and structural growth exposure and reducing concentrated single-stock positions.
UBS also suggests capital preservation strategies for risk-averse investors, especially those with concentrated positions, large gains or near-term liquidity needs.

Fixed income rebounded in October. The Bloomberg US Treasury Index gained 2.4% (down 0.5% YTD) and European government bonds rose 0.9% (down 1.4% YTD). French 10-year yields hit their highest since 2002 on political uncertainty. UBS stays Attractive on fixed income, favoring short- to medium-duration quality bonds with selective extension toward the 10-year area, and is cautious on the longest maturities.
Credit: US investment grade gained 2.1%, Euro IG 0.8%, US high yield 0.6% (only positive YTD fixed-income segment at +0.5%), Euro high yield fell 0.8% on spread widening.
Regional equities: MSCI Switzerland +6.8% (15.1% YTD), MSCI UK +1.5% (11.3% YTD), MSCI China -7.1% (-18.0% YTD), MSCI Japan -4.0% (+18.5% YTD), MSCI EM -8.0% (+13.8% YTD).

Commodities: CMCI Brent index +13.0% (+88.7% YTD) on Middle East supply disruption and reports of possible renewed US-Iran escalation after the US midterms. Gold fell 6.6% (-10.7% YTD) on higher real yields and a stronger dollar. UBS favors broad commodities via active management.
UBS favors equity themes in Artificial intelligence, Power and resources, and Longevity.

sector_views.rationale: Positive on equities given resilient activity, healthy earnings growth and continued AI investment. Use weakness to build diversified structural growth exposure.
Rated Attractive. Elevated yields offer income and diversification, and quality bonds could gain if tightening expectations fade. Favors short- to medium-duration quality bonds.
Favors broad commodities for differentiated returns and protection when inflation pressures equities and bonds.
AI demand is robust but financing and monetization concerns may cause periodic volatility.

earnings_insights: UBS expects Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth of 25-30% (UBS estimate, not yet a reported figure).
Reported Q3 cloud results: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y, Microsoft Azure +48% y/y, and Microsoft large Copilot accounts up eightfold.
Cloud revenue growth accelerated across the largest providers, advance orders for computing capacity expanded and company guidance stayed positive.

Peak level in early October before yields fell on tech weakness, safe-haven demand and central banks holding rates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Mildly hawkish hold with growth assessment raised to 'strong'.

trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings and economic activity remain resilient despite higher yields and energy prices.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher rates, energy costs, geopolitical risks and uncertainty over AI monetization could cause volatility.

trade_ideas.description: Own short- to medium-duration high-quality bonds, with selective extension toward the 10-year area
trade_ideas.rationale: Repricing restored return potential, with a cushion against higher yields and upside if inflation or growth eases.
trade_ideas.risk: Fiscal concerns and elevated issuance on the longest maturities.

trade_ideas.description: Capital preservation strategies for investors with concentrated positions or low loss tolerance
trade_ideas.rationale: Limits the impact of a market drawdown while keeping equity exposure.

vol_and_positioning: Technology shares became more volatile in October on AI financing and monetization doubts. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% for the month, its worst since March 2025.
UBS suggests capital preservation strategies for investors with concentrated positions, large gains or low loss tolerance, to limit drawdown exposure while staying in equities.
geopolitical: Continued tensions and further attacks in the Middle East kept energy supply disruption risk in focus.
Reports of possible renewed US-Iran military escalation after the US midterm elections.
Political uncertainty in France pushed 10-year French government bond yields to highs not seen since 2002.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 cloud revenue accelerated (Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%), advance orders for compute expanded and guidance stayed positive. Most capex sits with larger, better-funded companies.
tension_points.bear_case: Overinvestment pressures free cash flow, financing relies increasingly on debt, equity, leases and supplier-backed funding, and new AI products may displace existing revenue before they monetize. Specialized AI cloud providers face higher borrowing costs and refinancing risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stress at indebted AI cloud providers broadening into a general reversal in AI spending, which UBS views as less likely than selective delays, repricing and consolidation.
